title: README, install docs, CHANGELOG and accessibility docs
owns: README.md (except the sign-in paragraph the agent package writes), docs/**, CHANGELOG.md

findings.title: README leaves Windows users blocked by Smart App Control with no way forward
findings.scenario: A user on a recent Windows 11 install (Smart App Control On) extracts the zip and starts Ember.exe. The README says SAC 'blocks unsigned apps outright and can't make an exception for one app' and stops. It doesn't say what the user will see, that SAC is under Windows Security › App & browser control › Smart App Control settings, that turning it off may be one-way on their build, or that they can use another computer or wait for a signed build. A home user cannot complete the install; an enterprise user is not told to ask IT.
findings.evidence: README.md:34-41; grep -rn 'Smart App Control' app finds only vocabulary.ts (no detection, no doctor row, no in-app wording); docs/DEVELOPING.md:588 only repeats that the README covers it.
findings.fix: Add the symptom (a 'Smart App Control blocked…' message with no Run anyway), the exact path to turn it off, the warning that turning it back on may need a Windows reset on some builds, and 'on a managed PC ask your administrator'. Better: sign the Windows build before release.

findings.title: README has no download location and the AppImage line omits the system packages it needs
findings.scenario: 'Get Ember-0.1.0-win-x64.zip' (and the mac dmg) points at 'npm run package:win' or a manual CI run whose artifact is kept for 3 days (ci.yml retention-days: 3); there is no release workflow and no link, so a non-developer cannot find the installer. The Linux line 'Or run Ember-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage without installing' omits that the AppImage needs the system packages the RPM pulls in (python3-pyatspi, python3-gobject, at-spi2-core…); without them the Setup check says only 'Python accessibility bindings are missing: sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi' (it omits python3-gobject, which the doctor lists) and Ember can't read apps.
findings.evidence: README.md:25, 29-30, 59-61; .github/workflows/ci.yml retention-days: 3 (no release job); packaging/rpm/ember.spec Requires list; app/main/environment.ts:174 vs app/main/doctor.ts:137.
findings.fix: Link the GitHub Releases page once the files are published (and list the checksums). For the AppImage, name the packages (`sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi python3-gobject at-spi2-core`) and make the Setup check's message match the doctor's.

findings.title: README's Gatekeeper steps stop at 'macOS 15'
findings.scenario: The README lists 'macOS 15:' (Open Anyway) and 'macOS 13 and 14:' (Control-click). Ember reads macOS 26 correctly (permissions.ts maps Darwin 25 to 26) and the README says '13 or later', but on macOS 26 a user doesn't know which line applies (the Open Anyway flow is the same as 15's).
findings.fix: Say 'macOS 15 and later' (and re-check the wording on macOS 26).

findings.title: README offers the AppImage "without installing" but it still needs the RPM's system packages
findings.scenario: A RHEL 8 user without python3-pyatspi (or Xvfb, speech-dispatcher...) runs the AppImage as the README suggests. Ember starts, but cannot read any app: the sidecar runs on the host's platform-python and the AppImage carries only the Electron side. The window shows setup-check failures. The README sentence gives no hint, and the doctor's speech-model fix text also says "or install ember-voice-models", an RPM that an AppImage user cannot use.
findings.evidence: The AppImage carries only dist/package/ember. python3-pyatspi, python3-gobject and at-spi2-core are RPM Requires (spec lines ~31-33), and the sidecar is spawned with the system Python (app/main/perception/sidecar.ts:186-190). My AppImage doctor run printed "warn Reading apps: Python accessibility bindings are missing" and "or install ember-voice-models".
findings.fix: Change the sentence to "... without installing Ember itself; it still needs `sudo dnf install python3-pyatspi python3-gobject at-spi2-core` (run `Ember.AppImage doctor`)". Drop the ember-voice-models hint when APPIMAGE is set.

findings.title: The SSH consent card, README, CHANGELOG and docs understate the helper's size; the install extracts the whole Node distribution
findings.area: docs/consent text vs code: SSH install
findings.scenario: The consent card the user clicks Connect on says 'about 31 MB, unpacked to about 125 MB in ~/.local/share/ember-remote'. Reality is larger, and different on a Mac. Users on small or NFS-quota homes and IT admins are surprised.
findings.evidence: Pinned Node 24.21.0 linux-x64: the tar.xz is 31,890,184 bytes (sha256 matches remote-runtime.json) plus 0.8 MB of parts, i.e. about 33 MB. The gz fallback used when the remote has no xz is 58,088,022 bytes. It unpacks to 208 MB (bin/node 121 MB, include/ 67 MB, lib/ 19 MB). The docs (COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:389-393) say 29 MB download and 125 MB unpacked. The card always names the Linux path even though macOS remotes install under ~/Library/Application Support/Ember Remote. The bootstrap untars everything with --strip-components=1.
findings.fix: Correct the numbers (about 33 MB, or 59 MB without xz; about 210 MB unpacked) in the card, README, CHANGELOG and docs. Exclude include/ and lib/node_modules from the extraction (saves roughly 80 MB). Make the card's path OS-neutral, or ask the OS first.

findings.title: Docs describe three behaviours the code doesn't have: a task-triggered commands card, a WSL offer on first sight, and Wayland remotes with controls
findings.scenario: A user or admin follows §2.1 'The first time you turn one on (or a task needs one), Ember shows the card…': with commands off (the default), run_command isn't even offered to the model, so no card ever comes from a task. §3.1 says 'When Ember first sees WSL it offers…': the offer only appears after the user's request names WSL while it is off. §1's table says an SSH Linux Wayland desktop gives 'reading and using controls': packaged builds never enable that, so Wayland remotes (the default on RHEL 8 and 9 GNOME and recent Ubuntu) are commands only.
findings.evidence: commandCapability returns 'off' when settings.commands[id].on is false (local-service.ts:53), and worker.commandShells() returns null for 'off' (worker.ts:963), so there is no run_command tool and no flow.ts step-2 card unless a card version was bumped. offerWsl() is called only from the bind path in runtime.ts:1279 when the user said 'in WSL'. app/remote/main.ts:205 sets `waylandText: !o.packaged && EMBER_REMOTE_WAYLAND === '1'`. §4.4 and L5 are right; the §1 table row (line 25) contradicts them.
findings.fix: Edit §2.1 ('the card appears when you turn the switch on in Settings'), §3.1 ('when you ask for something in WSL while it is off') and the §1 Wayland row ('none yet: commands only'). Do the same in CHANGELOG where it repeats them.

findings.title: No accessibility documentation: README and docs say nothing about screen-reader behaviour, keyboard routes or known gaps
findings.area: Screen reader compatibility notes (Orca, NVDA, Narrator, VoiceOver)
findings.scenario: A screen-reader or keyboard-only user cannot find which controls have a keyboard route, that the overlay and handle cannot be focused, that Ember speaks aloud when a screen reader runs, that Ctrl+Alt+X is the way to stop an announced command, how to read a command before allowing it (Alt+Tab to 'Ember commands'), or how to leave the desk and the terminal. Only a sentence in docs/DEVELOPING.md:129 and the settings 'Comfort and access' note mention it. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 do not list the terminal's missing screen-reader mode.
findings.evidence: grep -n -i 'screen reader|Orca|NVDA|Narrator|VoiceOver' README.md docs/*.md: only DEVELOPING.md:129 and DESIGN.md:78. PLAN.md manual item 14 is the only plan for testing Narrator, NVDA and VoiceOver.
findings.fix: Add an 'Accessibility' section to the README: per-OS reader notes, a keyboard-route table for every bubble, card, window and mouse-only action, speech behaviour, and the known gaps from this report.

findings.title: CHANGELOG is still "Unreleased" and covers only SSH, WSL and commands, not the Windows and macOS port
findings.scenario: The release candidate also contains the Windows and macOS ports (README documents installs for both), but the only release-notes section is "## Unreleased: commands, WSL and other computers". A "Changed" entry says Windows treated WSLg apps as Remote Desktop "before", though nothing earlier was ever released. Readers get no 0.1.0 heading or date.
findings.evidence: grep "^## " CHANGELOG.md gives one heading, line 3. README.md and package.json say 0.1.0.
findings.fix: Retitle to "0.1.0 (date)", open with the first-release summary (Linux, Windows and macOS, voice, characters), keep the new features as a section, and drop the "Changed" wording that refers to unreleased behaviour.

findings.title: docs/DESIGN.md says a character can be chosen in the handle menu; there is no such item
findings.scenario: "All four ship in the app and are chosen in setup, settings, the handle menu, or by voice." The handle menu has Ask Ember…, Stop everything, Work on, Mute, Read the last answer, Settings…, Stay put or Follow my cursor, Hide or Show Ember and Quit Ember, and no character picker.
findings.evidence: app/main/main.ts:529-548 (the whole menu template); no character or submenu entries, and grep for the character names in main.ts finds none in the menu.
findings.fix: Drop "the handle menu" from DESIGN.md, or add a character submenu.

findings.title: Linux has no uninstall guidance, and the autostart entry survives dnf remove
findings.scenario: A user who turned on "Start Ember when I log in" runs `sudo dnf remove ember`. ~/.config/autostart/ember.desktop stays and keeps pointing at /usr/bin/ember --autostart. ~/.config/ember (including github-token.bin, logs, audit and 126 MB of models), ~/Ember and the Node runtime for remotes also stay. README.md gives Windows and macOS removal steps listing exactly these paths; the Linux section has none.
findings.evidence: autostartEntry (autostart.ts:31-45) has Exec= but no TryExec=, so the desktop cannot skip a missing binary quietly. The RPM has no %preun/%postun cleanup of per-user files (rpm cannot reach home folders). README.md:10-25 (Linux) vs :52-56 and :86-90.
findings.fix: Add `TryExec=` (the same path as Exec's first word) to the autostart entry. Add a short "To remove Ember" paragraph to the Linux README: turn off start at login, `sudo dnf remove ember`, delete ~/.config/ember and ~/Ember.

findings.title: Removing Ember from a PC leaves its helper on every SSH computer, and the README removal steps do not mention it
findings.scenario: A user deletes the Ember folder (Windows) or app (macOS) following the README without clicking "Remove Ember from build-01" first. build-01 keeps ~/.local/share/ember-remote with the Node runtime and parts, and per-machine consent, lock and audit files. The error text elsewhere says it needs about 400 MB, and nothing on the PC remains to remove it. The remote's README.txt tells an admin how to run uninstall.sh, but the person who set it up is never told.
findings.evidence: README.md:52-56 (Windows) and :86-90 (macOS) list the shortcut, login item and data folder, but not remote computers. CHANGELOG notes "Remove Ember from build-01 removes the helper again". uninstall.sh and the part's README.txt exist only on the remote.
findings.fix: Add "If you added computers over SSH, choose **Remove Ember from <computer>** for each before removing Ember (or run sh ~/.local/share/ember-remote/versions/*/uninstall.sh there)" to the removal paragraphs.

findings.title: docs/DEVELOPING.md §10.5 lists what the Windows folder holds but omits remote-parts, the WSL helper and the askpass source
findings.scenario: A maintainer or administrator checking an extracted zip against §10.5 finds resources\remote-parts, resources\sidecar\atspi\ember_atspi.py and resources\ssh\ember_askpass.cs and has no description of what they are, or whether they should be on an allow-list (they are compiled or run by Ember at use).
findings.evidence: layout.mjs:79-84 stages ember_atspi.py and ember_askpass.cs for win32 and stage.mjs:171-179 stages remote-parts. The §10.5 table names only sidecar\uia, ember.ico, ember-doctor.cmd and the notices.
findings.fix: Add the three entries to the table with one line each (WSL's Linux-app helper, the SSH password helper compiled on first use, the helper archives sent to SSH computers).
